story: Sosruko is a central character in many cycles of the Nart sagas of the North Caucasus. He is a powerful but devious man, though he is the smallest of the Narts, a people whose sagas recount many heroic deeds. Because of his cunning and his power despite his small stature, Sosruko is sometimes cast in the light of a trickster figure among his people. He is described as a minion of the gods, serving them in some capacity, and he is also the son of a doting mother, Lady Satanaya, who cares for him closely. The central deed attributed to Sosruko is that he stole fire from a giant. This act of theft, taking fire away from a being far larger and presumably more powerful than himself, stands as his defining accomplishment within the mythology of his people. His smallness in comparison to the other Narts makes this feat notable, since he achieves through cleverness and deviousness what might otherwise require great physical strength. His mother's devotion to him is mentioned alongside this feat, suggesting that his family relationship played a role in the stories told about him. Sosruko's identity as a trickster-like figure, his service to the gods, his relationship with his mother, and his theft of fire from the giant together form the core narrative elements associated with him in the Nart sagas, which are the traditional stories of the peoples of the North Caucasus region.
